source.text: וַנֵּ֣פֶן וַנַּ֔עַל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתֵ֜נוּ ה֧וּא וְכָל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And we turned and went up [the] way of the Bashan, and came out Og king of the Bashan to meet us, he and all his people, for the battle [at] Edrei.

en.L: And we turned and went up [by] the way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.
en.B: Then we turned and went up along the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us with all his army to do battle at Edrei.
en.R: Next we turned north and went up the road toward Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with his whole army to fight us at Edrei.

es.L: Y nos volvimos y subimos [por] el camino de Basán, y Og, rey de Basán, salió a nuestro encuentro, él y todo su pueblo, para la batalla en Edrei.
es.B: Luego dimos la vuelta y subimos por el camino de Basán, y Og, rey de Basán, salió contra nosotros con todo su ejército para presentar batalla en Edrei.
es.R: Después giramos hacia el norte y subimos por el camino que lleva a Basán. Og, el rey de Basán, salió con todo su ejército a pelear contra nosotros en Edrei.

fr.L: Et nous nous sommes tournés et nous sommes montés [par] le chemin du Bashân, et Og, roi du Bashân, est sorti à notre rencontre, lui et tout son peuple, pour la bataille à Édréï.
fr.B: Puis nous avons fait demi-tour et nous sommes montés par la route du Bashân, et Og, roi du Bashân, est sorti contre nous avec toute son armée pour livrer bataille à Édréï.
fr.R: Ensuite, nous avons tourné vers le nord et nous avons pris la route qui monte vers le Bashân. Og, le roi du Bashân, est sorti avec toute son armée pour nous combattre à Édréï.

sw.L: Na tukageuka tukapanda [kwa] njia ya Bashani, na Ogu mfalme wa Bashani akatoka kukutana nasi, yeye na watu wake wote, kwa vita huko Edrei.
sw.B: Kisha tuligeuka tukapanda kwa njia iendayo Bashani, na Ogu mfalme wa Bashani akatoka kupigana nasi pamoja na jeshi lake lote huko Edrei.
sw.R: Baadaye tuligeuka kuelekea kaskazini, tukapanda njia ya kwenda Bashani. Ogu, mfalme wa Bashani, akatoka na jeshi lake lote ili kupigana nasi huko Edrei.

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 방향을 돌려 바산 길로 올라갔는데, 바산 왕 옥이 우리를 맞아, 그와 그의 모든 백성이 에드레이에서 싸우려고 나왔다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 우리는 방향을 돌려 바산으로 가는 길로 올라갔다. 그러자 바산 왕 옥이 온 군대를 이끌고 에드레이로 나와 우리와 맞서 싸우려 했다.
ko.R: 그다음에 우리는 북쪽으로 방향을 돌려 바산으로 가는 길로 올라갔습니다. 그러자 바산 왕 옥이 온 군대를 이끌고 에드레이로 나와 우리와 싸우려 했습니다.

vi.L: Và chúng ta đã quay lại và đi lên [theo] đường Ba-san, và Óc, vua Ba-san, cùng toàn dân mình kéo ra đón đánh chúng ta, để giao chiến tại Ết-rê-i.
vi.B: Rồi chúng ta quay lại và đi lên theo con đường về Ba-san. Óc, vua Ba-san, cùng toàn quân kéo ra đánh chúng ta tại Ết-rê-i.
vi.R: Kế đến chúng ta quay lên phía bắc, đi theo con đường về Ba-san. Óc, vua Ba-san, cùng toàn quân của vua kéo ra đánh chúng ta tại Ết-rê-i.

decisions.choice: we turned, we went up: Moses goes on telling the journey, speaking for himself and Israel
decisions.reason: The chapter lies inside Moses' first speech (1:6-4:40). He is still recalling the march, which reached the land east of the Jordan in chapter 2. Verses 1-7 retell the victory over Og told in Numbers 21:33-35, in almost the same words.

decisions.choice: Bashan, Og, Edrei: the high country north of Gilead, its king, and a royal town on its southern edge
decisions.reason: Bashan was the fertile tableland east and north-east of the Sea of Galilee, known for its cattle and oaks (32:14; Isaiah 2:13). Og ruled it from Ashtaroth and Edrei (1:4; Joshua 12:4).

decisions.choice: to meet us ... all his people: to confront us in battle with all his fighting men
decisions.reason: "To meet" someone with an army and "for battle" means to march out against them. "His people" here are the men who fought for him, as in Numbers 21:33.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: Moses' first speech opened its quotation at 1:6 and closes it at 4:40. Records in between carry no outer quotation marks, and words that Moses quotes inside the speech take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: army; Readable "north"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army" for "his people" in battle. Readable adds "north", since the road to Bashan led north from the land of Sihon.

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level ("nous sommes montés", "est sorti")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As set for the whole of Deuteronomy at 1:1: the chapter is Moses speaking to the people and retelling the march, and a story told inside speech keeps the tenses of speech, so the passé composé is used at every level.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ לְסִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me, do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land, and you will do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorite[s] who [was] dwelling in Heshbon.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon.'
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, together with all his army and his land. Treat him as you treated Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.'
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him. I have already given him, his whole army and his land into your power. Do the same to him as you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon.'

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: “No le temas, porque en tu mano lo he entregado, a él y a todo su pueblo y su tierra; y harás con él como hiciste con Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que habitaba en Hesbón.”
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: “No tengas miedo de él, porque te lo he entregado junto con todo su ejército y su tierra. Trátalo como trataste a Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que reinaba en Hesbón.”
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: “No le tengas miedo. Ya he puesto en tu poder a él, a todo su ejército y su tierra. Haz con él lo mismo que hiciste con Sijón, el rey amorreo que gobernaba desde Hesbón.”

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : “Ne le crains pas, car dans ta main je l’ai livré, lui et tout son peuple et son pays ; et tu lui feras comme tu as fait à Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui habitait à Heshbon.”
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : “N’aie pas peur de lui, car je te l’ai livré, avec toute son armée et son pays. Traite-le comme tu as traité Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui régnait à Heshbon.”
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : “N’aie pas peur de lui. Je l’ai déjà mis en ton pouvoir, lui, toute son armée et son pays. Fais-lui ce que tu as fait à Sihon, le roi amoréen qui régnait depuis Heshbon.”

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, 'Usimwogope, kwa maana nimemtia mkononi mwako, yeye na watu wake wote na nchi yake; nawe utamtendea kama ulivyomtendea Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyekaa Heshboni.'
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniambia, 'Usimwogope, kwa maana nimemtia mikononi mwako pamoja na jeshi lake lote na nchi yake. Umtendee kama ulivyomtendea Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala Heshboni.'
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniambia, 'Usimwogope. Tayari nimemweka yeye, jeshi lake lote na nchi yake chini ya mamlaka yako. Mfanyie kama ulivyomfanyia Sihoni, mfalme wa Waamori aliyetawala kutoka Heshboni.'

ko.L: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. '그를 두려워하지 말라. 내가 그와 그의 모든 백성과 그의 땅을 네 손에 넘겨주었다. 너는 헤스본에 살던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼에게 한 것처럼 그에게도 할 것이다.'
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. '그를 두려워하지 말라. 내가 그와 그의 온 군대와 그의 땅을 너에게 넘겨주었다. 헤스본에서 다스리던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼에게 한 것처럼 그에게도 하여라.'
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 저에게 말씀하셨습니다. '그를 두려워하지 말라. 내가 이미 그와 그의 온 군대와 그의 땅을 네 손에 넘겨주었다. 헤스본에서 다스리던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼에게 한 것처럼 그에게도 똑같이 하여라.'

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: 'Chớ sợ nó, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phó nó, toàn dân nó và đất nó vào tay ngươi; và ngươi sẽ làm cho nó như ngươi đã làm cho Si-hôn, vua người A-mô-rít, là người ở tại Hết-bôn.'
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: 'Đừng sợ vua ấy, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phó vua cùng toàn quân và đất của vua vào tay con. Hãy đối xử với vua như con đã đối xử với Si-hôn, vua người A-mô-rít, đóng đô tại Hết-bôn.'
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: 'Đừng sợ vua ấy. Ta đã trao vua, toàn quân của vua và đất của vua vào tay con rồi. Hãy làm cho vua như con đã làm cho Si-hôn, vua người A-mô-rít cai trị từ Hết-bôn.'

decisions.choice: I have given: the victory is spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act. God speaks of the outcome as settled before the battle begins, as he did of Sihon (2:24, 31).

decisions.choice: into your hand: into your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control. "Your" is singular: God speaks to Moses as the leader who stands for the whole people.

decisions.choice: dwelling in Heshbon: living there as its ruler
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or to dwell, and of a king it can mean to sit on the throne, to reign. Heshbon was Sihon's royal city (2:24-36; Numbers 21:26).

decisions.choice: ruled
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ruled", since a king who "dwells" in a city reigns there. Literal keeps "dwelt".

decisions.choice: "nó" (L); "vua" (B, R) for Og in God's words
decisions.reason: God speaks of an enemy king; Literal uses the plain third person "nó", as the Hebrew "him"; Balanced and Readable call him "vua", the way Vietnamese narration speaks of a king.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ בְּיָדֵ֗נוּ גַּ֛ם אֶת־ע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֖ן וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֑וֹ וַנַּכֵּ֕הוּ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Yahweh our God into our hand also Og king of the Bashan and all his people, and we struck him until not he left to him [a] survivor.

en.L: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God gave into our hand Og king of Bashan also, and all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God handed Og king of Bashan and all his army over to us as well, and we struck him down until not one survivor was left to him.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God let us defeat King Og of Bashan and his whole army too. We fought them until no one was left alive.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios entregó en nuestra mano también a Og, rey de Basán, y a todo su pueblo, y lo herimos hasta no dejarle sobreviviente.
es.B: Así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos entregó también a Og, rey de Basán, con todo su ejército, y lo derrotamos hasta que no le quedó ni un solo sobreviviente.
es.R: Así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos dio también la victoria sobre Og, rey de Basán, y todo su ejército. Peleamos contra ellos hasta que no quedó nadie con vida.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu a livré aussi dans notre main Og, roi du Bashân, et tout son peuple, et nous l’avons frappé jusqu’à ne pas lui laisser de survivant.
fr.B: Ainsi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu nous a livré aussi Og, roi du Bashân, avec toute son armée, et nous l’avons battu jusqu’à ce qu’il ne lui reste plus un seul survivant.
fr.R: Ainsi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu nous a donné la victoire sur le roi Og du Bashân et sur toute son armée. Nous les avons combattus jusqu’à ce qu’il n’en reste plus un seul vivant.

sw.L: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu akamtia mkononi mwetu pia Ogu mfalme wa Bashani, na watu wake wote, nasi tukampiga hadi hakubakiwa na mtu aliyenusurika.
sw.B: Hivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu akamtia pia Ogu mfalme wa Bashani mikononi mwetu, pamoja na jeshi lake lote, nasi tukampiga hadi hakubakiwa na mtu hata mmoja aliyenusurika.
sw.R: Hivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu alituwezesha kumshinda pia Mfalme Ogu wa Bashani na jeshi lake lote. Tulipigana nao mpaka hakuna hata mmoja aliyebaki hai.

ko.L: 그래서 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 바산 왕 옥과 그의 모든 백성도 우리 손에 넘겨주셨으니, 우리는 그를 쳐서 그에게 살아남은 자가 하나도 남지 않게 했다.
ko.B: 이렇게 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 바산 왕 옥과 그의 온 군대도 우리에게 넘겨주셨다. 우리는 그를 쳐서 살아남은 사람이 하나도 없게 했다.
ko.R: 이렇게 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리가 바산 왕 옥과 그의 온 군대도 무찌르게 해 주셨습니다. 우리는 그들과 싸워서 한 사람도 살아남지 못하게 했습니다.

vi.L: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta cũng đã phó vào tay chúng ta Óc, vua Ba-san, cùng toàn dân vua, và chúng ta đánh giết vua cho đến khi không còn ai sống sót cho vua.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta cũng phó Óc, vua Ba-san, cùng toàn quân vào tay chúng ta, và chúng ta đánh giết vua cho đến khi không còn một người nào của vua sống sót.
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta cũng cho chúng ta đánh bại Óc, vua Ba-san, và toàn quân của vua. Chúng ta đánh họ cho đến khi không còn ai sống sót.

decisions.choice: also: Og falls as Sihon had
decisions.reason: "Also" ties this victory to the one over Sihon (2:33). The two kings fall in the same way, and the next verses tell it in the same pattern (2:34-36).

decisions.choice: until he left no survivor: until no one was left
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It can be read "until one left him no survivor", meaning simply that none of Og's forces were left alive (Numbers 21:35).

decisions.choice: struck: struck down in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike, and in battle to defeat and kill.

decisions.choice: let us defeat
decisions.reason: Readable says what "gave into our hand" means: the LORD gave Israel the victory.

source.text: וַנִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת־כָּל־עָרָיו֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לֹ֤א הָֽיְתָה֙ קִרְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־לָקַ֖חְנוּ מֵֽאִתָּ֑ם שִׁשִּׁ֥ים עִיר֙ כָּל־חֶ֣בֶל אַרְגֹּ֔ב מַמְלֶ֥כֶת ע֖וֹג בַּבָּשָֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And we captured all his cities at the time the that; not there was [a] town which not we took from them: sixty cities, all [the] region of Argob, [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan.

en.L: And we captured all his cities at that time; there was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
en.B: At that time we captured all his towns. There was not a single town we failed to take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, Og's kingdom in Bashan.
en.R: At that time we captured every one of his towns. There was not one town we did not take. There were sixty towns in all. They were in the whole area of Argob, which was Og's kingdom in Bashan.

es.L: Y tomamos todas sus ciudades en aquel tiempo; no hubo ciudad que no les tomáramos: sesenta ciudades, toda la región de Argob, el reino de Og en Basán.
es.B: En aquel tiempo conquistamos todas sus poblaciones. No quedó ni una que no les quitáramos: sesenta poblaciones, toda la región de Argob, el reino de Og en Basán.
es.R: En ese tiempo capturamos todos sus pueblos. No hubo ni uno que no tomáramos. Eran sesenta pueblos en total, en toda la zona de Argob, que era el reino de Og en Basán.

fr.L: Et nous avons pris toutes ses villes en ce temps-là ; il n’y a pas eu de cité que nous ne leur ayons prise : soixante villes, toute la région d’Argob, le royaume d’Og dans le Bashân.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, nous avons pris toutes ses villes. Aucune ne nous a échappé : soixante villes, toute la région d’Argob, le royaume d’Og dans le Bashân.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, nous avons pris toutes ses villes, sans exception. Il y en avait soixante en tout. Elles se trouvaient dans toute la région d’Argob, qui était le royaume d’Og dans le Bashân.

sw.L: Nasi tukaiteka miji yake yote wakati ule; hapakuwa na mji ambao hatukuutwaa kwao: miji sitini, eneo lote la Argobu, ufalme wa Ogu katika Bashani.
sw.B: Wakati huo tuliteka miji yake yote. Hapakuwa na mji hata mmoja ambao hatukuwanyang'anya: miji sitini, eneo lote la Argobu, ufalme wa Ogu huko Bashani.
sw.R: Wakati huo tuliteka kila mji wake. Hakuna mji hata mmoja ambao hatukuuteka. Ilikuwa miji sitini kwa jumla, katika eneo lote la Argobu, yaani ufalme wa Ogu huko Bashani.

ko.L: 그리고 그때에 우리는 그의 모든 성읍을 점령했다. 우리가 그들에게서 빼앗지 않은 성읍이 하나도 없었으니, 육십 성읍, 곧 아르곱 온 지역, 바산에 있는 옥의 나라였다.
ko.B: 그때에 우리는 그의 성읍을 모두 점령했다. 우리가 빼앗지 못한 성읍은 하나도 없었다. 그것은 육십 개 성읍으로, 아르곱 온 지역, 곧 바산에 있는 옥의 나라였다.
ko.R: 그때에 우리는 그의 성읍을 하나도 빠짐없이 모두 점령했습니다. 우리가 빼앗지 못한 성읍은 하나도 없었습니다. 모두 예순 개 성읍이었습니다. 그 성읍들은 아르곱 온 지역에 있었는데, 그곳이 바산에 있는 옥의 나라였습니다.

vi.L: Và vào lúc ấy chúng ta đã chiếm tất cả các thành của vua; không có thành nào chúng ta không lấy của họ: sáu mươi thành, cả miền Ạt-gốp, vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san.
vi.B: Lúc ấy chúng ta chiếm tất cả các thành của vua. Không có một thành nào chúng ta không chiếm được: sáu mươi thành, cả miền Ạt-gốp, tức là vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san.
vi.R: Lúc ấy chúng ta chiếm hết mọi thành của vua. Không có thành nào chúng ta không chiếm. Tất cả có sáu mươi thành. Các thành ấy ở khắp miền Ạt-gốp, là vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san.

decisions.choice: the region of Argob: a district of Bashan
decisions.reason: The word for "region" first means a cord or measuring line, and so a stretch of land measured off. Argob was a district within Bashan, named again in verses 13-14 and 1 Kings 4:13. Its exact borders are not known.

decisions.choice: not a town that we did not take: every town, without exception
decisions.reason: The double negative makes a strong statement: every one of Og's towns was taken.

decisions.choice: at that time: the time of these events
decisions.reason: The phrase runs through Moses' retelling (verses 8, 12, 18, 21, 23; 2:34) and marks what happened during the march, as he looks back on it.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:2, Literal says "cities" and Balanced and Readable "towns", since these were mostly small walled places.

decisions.choice: "Ạt-gốp"
decisions.reason: The form of 1 Kings 4:13 for the same region.

source.text: כָּל־אֵ֜לֶּה עָרִ֧ים בְּצֻר֛וֹת חוֹמָ֥ה גְבֹהָ֖ה דְּלָתַ֣יִם וּבְרִ֑יחַ לְבַ֛ד מֵעָרֵ֥י הַפְּרָזִ֖י הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: All these [were] cities fortified [with] wall high, [double] doors and bar, apart from [the] cities of the open-country [dwellers], very many.

en.L: All these [were] cities fortified [with] high walls, doors and bars, besides the towns of the open country, very many.
en.B: Every one of these towns was fortified with high walls and with barred double gates, and there were very many open villages besides.
en.R: All these towns had strong defenses, with high walls and gates that could be barred shut. There were also a great many villages without walls.

es.L: Todas estas [eran] ciudades fortificadas [con] altas murallas, puertas y cerrojos, además de las poblaciones del campo abierto, muchísimas.
es.B: Todas estas poblaciones estaban fortificadas con altas murallas y con puertas dobles atrancadas, y había además muchísimas aldeas sin murallas.
es.R: Todos esos pueblos tenían fuertes defensas, con murallas altas y puertas que se podían cerrar con una tranca. Además había muchísimas aldeas sin murallas.

fr.L: Toutes celles-ci [étaient] des villes fortifiées [de] hautes murailles, de portes et de barres, outre les villes de la campagne ouverte, très nombreuses.
fr.B: Toutes ces villes étaient fortifiées de hautes murailles et de portes à deux battants fermées par des barres, et il y avait en outre de très nombreux villages sans remparts.
fr.R: Toutes ces villes avaient de solides défenses, avec de hauts murs et des portes qu’on pouvait bloquer avec une barre. Il y avait aussi beaucoup de villages sans murailles.

sw.L: Hii yote [ilikuwa] miji yenye ngome, [yenye] kuta ndefu, malango na makomeo, mbali na miji ya nchi wazi, mingi sana.
sw.B: Miji hiyo yote ilikuwa imejengewa ngome za kuta ndefu na malango ya milango miwili yenye makomeo, na zaidi ya hiyo kulikuwa na vijiji vingi sana visivyo na kuta.
sw.R: Miji hiyo yote ilikuwa na ulinzi imara, yenye kuta ndefu na malango yaliyoweza kufungwa kwa komeo. Pia kulikuwa na vijiji vingi sana visivyo na kuta.

ko.L: 이 모든 성읍은 높은 성벽과 문들과 빗장으로 견고하게 된 성읍들이었고, 그 밖에도 성벽 없는 마을들이 매우 많았다.
ko.B: 이 성읍들은 모두 높은 성벽과 빗장 지른 두 짝 문으로 튼튼하게 둘러싸여 있었고, 그 밖에도 성벽 없는 마을이 아주 많았다.
ko.R: 이 성읍들은 모두 튼튼하게 지어져 있었습니다. 높은 성벽이 있었고, 빗장을 질러 잠글 수 있는 성문이 있었습니다. 그 밖에도 성벽이 없는 마을이 아주 많았습니다.

vi.L: Tất cả những thành ấy [đều là] thành kiên cố, [có] tường cao, cửa và then, ngoài ra còn rất nhiều thành của dân quê [không có tường].
vi.B: Tất cả các thành ấy đều kiên cố, có tường cao, cổng hai cánh và then cài; ngoài ra còn rất nhiều làng mạc không có tường bao quanh.
vi.R: Tất cả các thành ấy đều được phòng thủ vững chắc, có tường cao và cổng có then cài chặt. Ngoài ra còn rất nhiều làng không có tường thành.

decisions.choice: doors and bar: gates of two leaves closed with a bar
decisions.reason: The word for "doors" is in the form used for pairs: a city gate had two leaves, and a beam was set across them to lock them (Judges 16:3; 1 Kings 4:13).

decisions.choice: the open country: unwalled settlements
decisions.reason: The word describes people who live in the open, in places without walls (Esther 9:19; Ezekiel 38:11). These are the farming villages around the walled towns.

decisions.choice: besides ... very many: these villages were taken too
decisions.reason: "Apart from" adds the villages to the sixty walled towns: Israel took both.

decisions.choice: barred double gates; open villages
decisions.reason: Balanced says "barred double gates" for the doors and bar of a city gate, and "open villages" for "the towns of the open country"; Readable says "villages without walls".

source.text: וַנַּחֲרֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ינוּ לְסִיחֹ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן הַחֲרֵם֙ כָּל־עִ֣יר מְתִ֔ם הַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And we devoted to destruction them as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting to destruction every city of men, the women and the little ones.

en.L: And we devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting to destruction every city: men, the women and the little ones.
en.B: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town to destruction, men, women and children.
en.R: We destroyed them completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as we had done to King Sihon of Heshbon. We destroyed every town and its men, women and children.

es.L: Y los consagramos a la destrucción, como habíamos hecho con Sijón, rey de Hesbón, consagrando a la destrucción toda ciudad: hombres, las mujeres y los niños.
es.B: Los consagramos a la destrucción, como habíamos hecho con Sijón, rey de Hesbón: consagramos a la destrucción cada población, hombres, mujeres y niños.
es.R: Los destruimos por completo, como algo entregado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, igual que habíamos hecho con el rey Sijón de Hesbón. Destruimos cada pueblo con sus hombres, mujeres y niños.

fr.L: Et nous les avons voués à la destruction, comme nous l’avions fait à Sihon, roi de Heshbon, vouant à la destruction chaque ville : hommes, les femmes et les petits enfants.
fr.B: Nous les avons voués à la destruction, comme nous l’avions fait pour Sihon, roi de Heshbon : nous avons voué à la destruction chaque ville, hommes, femmes et enfants.
fr.R: Nous les avons entièrement détruits, comme une chose livrée {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, comme nous l’avions fait au roi Sihon de Heshbon. Nous avons détruit chaque ville, avec ses hommes, ses femmes et ses enfants.

sw.L: Nasi tukawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, kama tulivyomtendea Sihoni mfalme wa Heshboni, tukiweka wakfu kwa maangamizi kila mji: wanaume, wanawake na watoto wadogo.
sw.B: Tuliwaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, kama tulivyomtendea Sihoni mfalme wa Heshboni; tuliweka wakfu kwa maangamizi kila mji, wanaume, wanawake na watoto.
sw.R: Tuliwaangamiza kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama tulivyomfanyia Mfalme Sihoni wa Heshboni. Tuliangamiza kila mji pamoja na wanaume wake, wanawake na watoto.

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 헤스본 왕 시혼에게 한 것처럼 그들을 진멸했으니, 모든 성읍의 남자들과 여자들과 어린것들을 진멸했다.
ko.B: 우리는 헤스본 왕 시혼에게 한 것처럼 그들을 진멸했다. 성읍마다 남자와 여자와 아이들까지 모두 진멸했다.
ko.R: 우리는 헤스본 왕 시혼에게 한 것처럼 그들을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바쳐 완전히 멸했습니다. 성읍마다 남자와 여자와 아이들까지 모두 그렇게 했습니다.

vi.L: Và chúng ta đã tận diệt chúng, như chúng ta đã làm cho Si-hôn, vua Hết-bôn, tận diệt mọi thành: đàn ông, đàn bà và trẻ nhỏ.
vi.B: Chúng ta tận diệt các thành ấy như đã làm với Si-hôn, vua Hết-bôn: tận diệt mọi thành, cả đàn ông, đàn bà lẫn trẻ em.
vi.R: Chúng ta hủy diệt hoàn toàn các thành ấy như những vật đã dâng hiến cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, như chúng ta đã làm với Si-hôn, vua Hết-bôn. Chúng ta hủy diệt mọi thành cùng đàn ông, đàn bà và trẻ em trong đó.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give over to God completely, keeping nothing
decisions.reason: This is the verb for a "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29): something given over to the LORD for good. In war it means the people of a town are put to death and none are kept as captives, as with Sihon (2:34). The law for the wars in the land is set out in 7:1-5 and 20:16-18.

decisions.choice: devoting to destruction: the verb repeated in its plain form
decisions.reason: The second verb is an infinitive that restates the first, stressing that the act was carried out on every town.

decisions.choice: men: the adult males of each town
decisions.reason: The word is a rare poetic word for men. With "the women and the little ones" it names the whole population of each town, as in 2:34.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:2, Readable gives the sense of "devote to destruction" in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the term.

source.text: וְכָל־הַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּשְׁלַ֥ל הֶעָרִ֖ים בַּזּ֥וֹנוּ לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the livestock and [the] spoil of the cities we plundered for ourselves.

en.L: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
en.B: The livestock, though, and the goods taken from the towns we kept as plunder for ourselves.
en.R: But we kept all the animals and the valuable things from the towns for ourselves.

es.L: Pero todo el ganado y el botín de las ciudades lo saqueamos para nosotros.
es.B: En cambio, el ganado y los bienes tomados de las poblaciones nos los quedamos como botín.
es.R: Pero nos quedamos con todos los animales y las cosas de valor de los pueblos.

fr.L: Mais tout le bétail et le butin des villes, nous l’avons pillé pour nous.
fr.B: Le bétail, en revanche, et les biens pris dans les villes, nous les avons gardés pour nous comme butin.
fr.R: Mais nous avons gardé pour nous tous les animaux et les objets de valeur des villes.

sw.L: Lakini mifugo yote na nyara za miji tulijitekea wenyewe.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, mifugo na mali tuliyoichukua katika miji tulijiwekea kuwa nyara.
sw.R: Lakini tulijichukulia wanyama wote na vitu vya thamani kutoka katika miji hiyo.

ko.L: 그러나 모든 가축과 성읍들의 전리품은 우리가 우리 것으로 빼앗았다.
ko.B: 그러나 가축과 성읍들에서 거둔 전리품은 우리가 가졌다.
ko.R: 그러나 짐승들과 성읍들에 있던 값진 물건들은 우리가 가졌습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng tất cả súc vật và chiến lợi phẩm của các thành, chúng ta đã cướp lấy cho mình.
vi.B: Còn súc vật và của cải lấy được từ các thành thì chúng ta giữ lại làm chiến lợi phẩm cho mình.
vi.R: Nhưng chúng ta giữ lại cho mình mọi súc vật và những của cải khác lấy được từ các thành.

decisions.choice: livestock and spoil: kept, as with Sihon
decisions.reason: In this war the ban applied to the people, but the animals and goods could be taken as plunder, as in 2:35. In other cases even these were given over to the LORD (Joshua 6:17-19).

decisions.choice: and all the livestock: placed first for contrast
decisions.reason: The objects stand at the head of the sentence, setting what was kept against the people who were destroyed in verse 6.

decisions.choice: the valuable things
decisions.reason: Readable says "valuable things" for the spoil: the goods taken from a captured town.

source.text: וַנִּקַּ֞ח בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִוא֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ מִיַּ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִנַּ֥חַל אַרְנֹ֖ן עַד־הַ֥ר חֶרְמֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And we took at the time the that the land from [the] hand of [the] two kings of the Amorite[s] who [were] beyond the Jordan, from [the] wadi of Arnon to [the] mountain of Hermon,

en.L: And we took at that time the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan, from the wadi of Arnon to Mount Hermon.
en.B: So at that time we took the land of the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
en.R: So at that time we took the land east of the Jordan River from the two Amorite kings. It stretched from the Arnon River in the south to Mount Hermon in the north.

es.L: Y tomamos en aquel tiempo la tierra de la mano de los dos reyes de los amorreos que [estaban] al otro lado del Jordán, desde el torrente del Arnón hasta el monte Hermón.
es.B: Así, en aquel tiempo tomamos la tierra de los dos reyes amorreos al otro lado del Jordán, desde el valle del Arnón hasta el monte Hermón.
es.R: Así, en ese tiempo les quitamos a los dos reyes amorreos la tierra que está al este del río Jordán. Iba desde el río Arnón en el sur hasta el monte Hermón en el norte.

fr.L: Et nous avons pris en ce temps-là le pays de la main des deux rois des Amoréens qui [étaient] au-delà du Jourdain, depuis le torrent de l’Arnon jusqu’au mont Hermon.
fr.B: Ainsi, en ce temps-là, nous avons pris le pays des deux rois amoréens au-delà du Jourdain, de la vallée de l’Arnon jusqu’au mont Hermon.
fr.R: Ainsi, à ce moment-là, nous avons pris aux deux rois amoréens le pays situé à l’est du Jourdain. Il s’étendait de la rivière Arnon, au sud, jusqu’au mont Hermon, au nord.

sw.L: Nasi tukaitwaa wakati ule nchi kutoka mkononi mwa wafalme wawili wa Waamori waliokuwa ng'ambo ya Yordani, kutoka korongo la Arnoni hadi mlima Hermoni.
sw.B: Hivyo wakati huo tuliitwaa nchi ya wafalme wawili wa Waamori ng'ambo ya Yordani, kutoka Bonde la Arnoni hadi Mlima Hermoni.
sw.R: Hivyo wakati huo tuliwanyang'anya wafalme wawili wa Waamori nchi iliyo upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani. Ilienea kutoka Mto Arnoni upande wa kusini hadi Mlima Hermoni upande wa kaskazini.

ko.L: 그리고 그때에 우리는 요단 건너편에 있던 아모리 사람의 두 왕의 손에서 그 땅을, 아르논 골짜기에서부터 헤르몬 산까지 빼앗았다.
ko.B: 이렇게 그때에 우리는 요단강 건너편에 있던 아모리 사람의 두 왕에게서 아르논 골짜기에서부터 헤르몬 산까지의 땅을 빼앗았다.
ko.R: 이렇게 그때에 우리는 아모리 사람의 두 왕에게서 요단강 동쪽 땅을 빼앗았습니다. 그 땅은 남쪽의 아르논 강에서부터 북쪽의 헤르몬 산까지였습니다.

vi.L: Và vào lúc ấy chúng ta đã lấy đất khỏi tay hai vua người A-mô-rít ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh, từ khe Ạt-nôn cho đến núi Hẹt-môn.
vi.B: Vậy lúc ấy chúng ta chiếm đất của hai vua người A-mô-rít ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh, từ thung lũng Ạt-nôn cho đến núi Hẹt-môn.
vi.R: Vậy lúc ấy chúng ta lấy được đất ở phía đông sông Giô-đanh từ tay hai vua người A-mô-rít. Đất ấy trải dài từ sông Ạt-nôn ở phía nam cho đến núi Hẹt-môn ở phía bắc.

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: on the east side of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual name for the land east of the river, seen from the land west of it (1:1, 5). Moses is speaking on the east side, so here it is a fixed name rather than his own viewpoint. In verses 20 and 25 the same words mean the west side, the land Israel has still to enter.

decisions.choice: from the Arnon to Hermon: the whole land east of the Jordan, south to north
decisions.reason: The Arnon runs west into the Dead Sea and was the southern border of Sihon's land (2:24, 36). Mount Hermon, the high mountain at the north end of the region, was the northern limit of Og's. The word for "wadi" names a stream in a valley and the valley it runs through.

decisions.choice: from the hand of: from the control of
decisions.reason: To take land "from the hand" of a king is to take it out of his power.

decisions.choice: east of the Jordan River; in the south ... in the north
decisions.reason: Readable says where "across the Jordan" lies from Moses' standpoint, and adds the directions so the reader can picture the extent of the land.

decisions.choice: "el torrente del Arnón" (L), "el valle del Arnón" (B), "el río Arnón" (R)
decisions.reason: The nachal is a stream with the valley it runs through. Literal "torrente" says a seasonal stream, Balanced follows the English "Valley" and Readable "River"; the same forms are used for the Arnon and the Jabbok in verses 12 and 16.

decisions.choice: "le torrent de l'Arnon" (L), "la vallée de l'Arnon" (B), "la rivière Arnon" (R)
decisions.reason: The nachal is a stream with the valley it runs through. French "torrent" is the usual word for a stream that runs in a steep valley and dries in summer; Balanced follows the English "Valley" and Readable "River", with "rivière" since the Arnon does not reach the sea. The same forms are used in verses 12 and 16.

decisions.choice: "korongo la Arnoni" (L), "Bonde la Arnoni" (B), "Mto Arnoni" (R)
decisions.reason: The nachal is a stream with the valley it runs through. Literal "korongo" (ravine) keeps the picture of a cut valley; Balanced follows the English "Valley" and Readable "River". The same forms are used in verses 12 and 16.

source.text: צִידֹנִ֛ים יִקְרְא֥וּ לְחֶרְמ֖וֹן שִׂרְיֹ֑ן וְהָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י יִקְרְאוּ־ל֖וֹ שְׂנִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorite[s] call it Senir.

en.L: (Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)

vi.L: (Người Si-đôn gọi Hẹt-môn là Si-ri-ôn, còn người A-mô-rít gọi nó là Sê-nia.)
vi.B: (Người Si-đôn gọi núi Hẹt-môn là Si-ri-ôn, còn người A-mô-rít gọi là Sê-nia.)
vi.R: (Dân thành Si-đôn gọi núi Hẹt-môn là Si-ri-ôn, còn người A-mô-rít gọi núi ấy là Sê-nia.)

decisions.choice: an aside inside Moses' speech
decisions.reason: The verse breaks off the list of conquered land to explain the other names of Hermon. Such notes stand inside Moses' speech here and in verses 11 and 13-14; the text does not say whether they are Moses' own words or a note added later for readers.

decisions.choice: Sirion, Senir: other peoples' names for Hermon
decisions.reason: The Sidonians were the Phoenicians of the coast to the north-west. "Sirion" is the name in Psalm 29:6, and "Senir" in 1 Chronicles 5:23, Song of Songs 4:8 and Ezekiel 27:5; Senir may sometimes name a peak of the Hermon range.

decisions.choice: parentheses
decisions.reason: The aside is set in parentheses at every level, so that the list of verses 8 and 10 can be read straight through. The outer quotation of Moses' speech stays open.

decisions.choice: "Hẹt-môn", "Si-ri-ôn", "Sê-nia"
decisions.reason: "Hẹt-môn" as Joshua 11-12 and "Si-ri-ôn" as Psalm 29:6; "Sê-nia" follows the same Protestant spelling.

records.literal_gloss: All [the] cities of the plateau and all the Gilead and all the Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, [the] cities of [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan.

en.L: All the cities of the plateau and all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
en.B: We captured every town of the plateau, the whole of Gilead and the whole of Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns that belonged to Og's kingdom in Bashan.
en.R: We took all the towns on the high plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as the towns of Salecah and Edrei. These were towns in Og's kingdom of Bashan.

es.L: Todas las ciudades de la meseta, y todo Galaad, y todo Basán, hasta Salca y Edrei, ciudades del reino de Og en Basán.
es.B: Conquistamos todas las poblaciones de la meseta, todo Galaad y todo Basán, hasta Salca y Edrei, poblaciones que pertenecían al reino de Og en Basán.
es.R: Tomamos todos los pueblos de la llanura alta, todo Galaad y todo Basán, hasta los pueblos de Salca y Edrei. Eran pueblos del reino de Og en Basán.

fr.L: Toutes les villes du plateau, et tout Galaad, et tout le Bashân, jusqu’à Salka et Édréï, villes du royaume d’Og dans le Bashân.
fr.B: Nous avons pris toutes les villes du plateau, tout Galaad et tout le Bashân, jusqu’à Salka et Édréï, villes qui appartenaient au royaume d’Og dans le Bashân.
fr.R: Nous avons pris toutes les villes du haut plateau, tout Galaad et tout le Bashân, jusqu’aux villes de Salka et d’Édréï. C’étaient des villes du royaume d’Og, dans le Bashân.

sw.L: Miji yote ya uwanda wa juu, na Gileadi yote, na Bashani yote, hadi Saleka na Edrei, miji ya ufalme wa Ogu katika Bashani.
sw.B: Tuliteka miji yote ya uwanda wa juu, Gileadi yote na Bashani yote, hadi Saleka na Edrei, miji iliyokuwa ya ufalme wa Ogu huko Bashani.
sw.R: Tulichukua miji yote ya nchi tambarare ya juu, Gileadi yote na Bashani yote, hadi miji ya Saleka na Edrei. Hiyo ilikuwa miji ya ufalme wa Ogu huko Bashani.

ko.L: 평원의 모든 성읍과 온 길르앗과, 살르가와 에드레이까지의 온 바산, 곧 바산에 있는 옥의 나라의 성읍들이다.
ko.B: 우리는 평원의 모든 성읍과 길르앗 전 지역과 살르가와 에드레이까지의 바산 전 지역을 점령했다. 그것은 바산에 있던 옥의 나라에 속한 성읍들이었다.
ko.R: 우리는 높은 평원에 있는 모든 성읍과 길르앗 전체와, 살르가 성과 에드레이 성까지 바산 전체를 차지했습니다. 이것들은 바산에 있던 옥의 나라의 성읍들이었습니다.

vi.L: Tất cả các thành của cao nguyên, cả Ga-la-át và cả Ba-san, cho đến Sanh-ca và Ết-rê-i, là các thành của vương quốc Óc ở Ba-san.
vi.B: Chúng ta chiếm mọi thành trên cao nguyên, cả miền Ga-la-át và cả miền Ba-san cho đến Sanh-ca và Ết-rê-i, là những thành thuộc vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san.
vi.R: Chúng ta chiếm tất cả các thành trên cao nguyên, cả miền Ga-la-át và cả miền Ba-san cho đến các thành Sanh-ca và Ết-rê-i. Đó là những thành trong vương quốc Ba-san của Óc.

decisions.choice: all the cities: the list goes on from verse 8
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb of its own. It spells out "the land" that Israel took (verse 8), after the aside of verse 9.

decisions.choice: the plateau, Gilead, Bashan: the three regions east of the Jordan, south to north
decisions.reason: The plateau is the high flat land north of the Arnon, Sihon's land (4:43; Joshua 13:9). Gilead is the hill country on both sides of the Jabbok, and Bashan the land north of it.

decisions.choice: Salecah and Edrei: the edges of Og's land
decisions.reason: Salecah lay at the eastern edge of Bashan (Joshua 13:11; 1 Chronicles 5:11), and Edrei on its south-western side (verse 1).

decisions.choice: We captured / We took
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb of verse 8, so the sentence stands on its own after the aside of verse 9.

source.text: כִּ֣י רַק־ע֞וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֗ן נִשְׁאַר֮ מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָרְפָאִים֒ הִנֵּ֤ה עַרְשׂוֹ֙ עֶ֣רֶשׂ בַּרְזֶ֔ל הֲלֹ֣ה הִ֔וא בְּרַבַּ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן תֵּ֧שַׁע אַמּ֣וֹת אָרְכָּ֗הּ וְאַרְבַּ֥ע אַמּ֛וֹת רָחְבָּ֖הּ בְּאַמַּת־אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: For only Og king of the Bashan was left from [the] remnant of the Rephaim; look, his bed [was a] bed of iron; [is] not it in Rabbah of [the] sons of Ammon? Nine cubits [is] its length and four cubits its width, by [the] cubit of [a] man.

en.L: (For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed [was] a bed of iron; [is] it not in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon? Nine cubits [is] its length and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man.)
en.B: (Og king of Bashan was the only one left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron, and it can still be seen in Rabbah of the Ammonites. It is {{units:about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide|nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the common cubit}}.)
en.R: (King Og of Bashan was the last one left of the Rephaim, a people known for their great size. His bed was made of iron, and you can still see it in the Ammonite city of Rabbah. It is {{units:about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide|nine cubits long and four cubits wide}}.)

es.L: (Porque solo Og, rey de Basán, había quedado del resto de los refaítas. He aquí, su lecho [era] un lecho de hierro; ¿no [está] en Rabá de los hijos de Amón? Nueve codos [es] su longitud y cuatro codos su anchura, según el codo de un hombre.)
es.B: (Og, rey de Basán, era el único que quedaba de los últimos refaítas. Su lecho era de hierro, y todavía se puede ver en Rabá de los amonitas. Mide {{units:unos 4 metros de largo y 1,80 metros de ancho|nueve codos de largo y cuatro codos de ancho, según el codo común}}.)
es.R: (El rey Og de Basán fue el último de los refaítas, un pueblo conocido por su gran estatura. Su cama era de hierro, y todavía se puede ver en Rabá, la ciudad de los amonitas. Mide {{units:unos 4 metros de largo y 1,80 metros de ancho|nueve codos de largo y cuatro codos de ancho}}.)

fr.L: (Car seul Og, roi du Bashân, était resté du reste des Rephaïm. Voici, son lit [était] un lit de fer ; n’est-il pas à Rabba des fils d’Ammon ? Neuf coudées [sont] sa longueur et quatre coudées sa largeur, selon la coudée d’un homme.)
fr.B: (Og, roi du Bashân, était le seul qui restait des derniers Rephaïm. Son lit était en fer, et on peut encore le voir à Rabba des Ammonites. Il mesure {{units:environ 4 mètres de long sur 1,80 mètre de large|neuf coudées de long sur quatre coudées de large, selon la coudée ordinaire}}.)
fr.R: (Le roi Og du Bashân était le dernier des Rephaïm, un peuple connu pour sa très grande taille. Son lit était en fer, et on peut encore le voir dans la ville ammonite de Rabba. Il mesure {{units:environ 4 mètres de long et 1,80 mètre de large|neuf coudées de long et quatre coudées de large}}.)

sw.L: (Kwa maana ni Ogu mfalme wa Bashani peke yake aliyebaki katika mabaki ya Warefai. Tazama, kitanda chake [kilikuwa] kitanda cha chuma; je, [hakimo] katika Raba ya wana wa Amoni? Dhiraa tisa [ndio] urefu wake na dhiraa nne upana wake, kwa dhiraa ya mtu.)
sw.B: (Ogu mfalme wa Bashani ndiye pekee aliyebaki katika mabaki ya Warefai. Kitanda chake kilikuwa cha chuma, na bado kinaweza kuonekana huko Raba ya Waamoni. {{units:Urefu wake ni karibu mita 4 na upana wake mita 1.80|Urefu wake ni dhiraa tisa na upana wake dhiraa nne, kwa dhiraa ya kawaida}}.)
sw.R: (Mfalme Ogu wa Bashani alikuwa wa mwisho wa Warefai, watu waliojulikana kwa kuwa warefu sana. Kitanda chake kilikuwa cha chuma, na bado unaweza kukiona katika mji wa Waamoni uitwao Raba. {{units:Urefu wake ni karibu mita 4 na upana wake ni mita 1.80|Urefu wake ni dhiraa tisa na upana wake ni dhiraa nne}}.)

ko.L: (르바임의 남은 자 가운데 바산 왕 옥만 남았기 때문이다. 보아라, 그의 침상은 쇠 침상이었으니, 그것이 암몬 자손의 랍바에 있지 않느냐? 사람의 규빗으로 그 길이가 아홉 규빗이요 그 너비가 네 규빗이다.)
ko.B: (바산 왕 옥은 르바임 가운데 마지막까지 남은 사람이었다. 그의 침상은 쇠로 만든 것이었는데, 지금도 암몬 사람들의 랍바에 있다. 그 크기는 {{units:길이가 4미터쯤, 너비가 1.8미터쯤|보통 규빗으로 길이가 아홉 규빗, 너비가 네 규빗}}이다.)
ko.R: (바산 왕 옥은 몸집이 큰 것으로 알려진 르바임 가운데 마지막까지 남은 사람이었습니다. 그의 침상은 쇠로 만든 것인데, 지금도 암몬 사람들의 성읍 랍바에 가면 볼 수 있습니다. 그 침상은 {{units:길이가 4미터쯤, 너비가 1.8미터쯤|길이가 아홉 규빗, 너비가 네 규빗}}입니다.)

vi.L: (Vì chỉ còn Óc, vua Ba-san, sót lại trong số những người Rê-pha-im còn sót. Kìa, giường của vua là một giường bằng sắt; [chẳng phải] nó ở tại Ráp-ba của con cháu Am-môn sao? Chiều dài của nó chín cu-đê và chiều rộng bốn cu-đê, theo cu-đê của người thường.)
vi.B: (Óc, vua Ba-san, là người duy nhất còn sót lại của dân Rê-pha-im. Giường của vua làm bằng sắt, và hiện vẫn còn ở Ráp-ba của người Am-môn. Giường ấy dài {{units:khoảng 4 m, rộng 1,8 m|chín cu-đê, rộng bốn cu-đê, theo cu-đê thông thường}}.)
vi.R: (Óc, vua Ba-san, là người cuối cùng còn lại của dân Rê-pha-im, một dân nổi tiếng to lớn. Giường của vua làm bằng sắt, và đến nay anh em vẫn có thể thấy nó tại thành Ráp-ba của người Am-môn. Giường ấy dài {{units:khoảng 4 m, rộng 1,8 m|chín cu-đê, rộng bốn cu-đê}}.)

decisions.choice: for only Og ...: an aside on Og
decisions.reason: Like verse 9, the verse breaks into the account to explain why Og was remembered. It speaks from a time when the bed was on show in Rabbah, so it may be a note for later readers.

decisions.choice: the remnant of the Rephaim: an ancient people known for their height
decisions.reason: The Rephaim were an old population of the land, remembered as tall and strong (2:10-11, 20-21; Genesis 14:5). Og was the last of them east of the Jordan (Joshua 12:4; 13:12).

decisions.choice: a bed of iron: a bed or couch, made of iron or of dark stone
decisions.reason: The word means a bed or couch (Amos 6:4; Psalm 6:7), and the verse probably describes a great bed of state. Some take it as a coffin, since large stone coffins have been found in the region. "Iron" may also describe the black basalt of Bashan, which looks like iron. Iron was costly at this time, so an iron bed would itself be a mark of power.

decisions.choice: nine cubits by four, by a man's cubit: about 13 1/2 by 6 feet
decisions.reason: "The cubit of a man" is the ordinary cubit, the length of a man's forearm, about 18 inches. The bed was about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide, far larger than a man needs.

decisions.choice: is it not in Rabbah?: it is there still
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes and points the hearer to something that could be seen. Rabbah was the chief city of the Ammonites (2 Samuel 12:26), where Amman stands today.

decisions.choice: about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the cubits as the setting alternative. Literal keeps the cubits.

decisions.choice: it can still be seen / you can still see it; Readable "a people known for their great size"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into a plain statement of what it means. Readable says who the Rephaim were, from 2:10-11.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 4 metros de largo y 1,80 metros de ancho|nueve codos de largo y cuatro codos de ancho}}
decisions.reason: Spanish gives the metric measure by default, at 45 cm to the cubit (9 x 45 cm = 4.05 m; 4 x 45 cm = 1.80 m), with the cubits as the setting alternative. Literal keeps the cubits, as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 4 mètres de long sur 1,80 mètre de large|neuf coudées de long sur quatre coudées de large}}
decisions.reason: French gives the metric measure by default, at 45 cm to the cubit (9 x 45 cm = 4.05 m; 4 x 45 cm = 1.80 m), with the cubits as the setting alternative. Literal keeps the cubits, as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{units:Urefu wake ni karibu mita 4 na upana wake mita 1.80|Urefu wake ni dhiraa tisa na upana wake dhiraa nne}}
decisions.reason: Swahili gives the metric measure by default, at 45 cm to the cubit, with the cubits (dhiraa) as the setting alternative. The span takes in the whole clause, since Swahili puts "urefu" and "upana" before the numbers. Literal keeps the cubits, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "khoảng 4 m, rộng 1,8 m" (metric); "chín cu-đê, rộng bốn cu-đê" (alternative)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese gives metric by default, with the cubit at 45 cm as the measures note sets; the English default is in feet. Literal keeps the cubits, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "Ráp-ba"
decisions.reason: The form of Joshua 13:25 for Rabbah of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: A units span in metres by default, with the cubits as the alternative; nine cubits about 4 m, four cubits about 1.8 m
decisions.reason: Korean readers measure in metres, so the default is metric (cubit 45 cm, as the Pentateuch sheets set), unlike the English feet; Literal keeps the cubits, as the English does.

source.text: וְאֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את יָרַ֖שְׁנוּ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑וא מֵעֲרֹעֵ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־עַל־נַ֣חַל אַרְנֹ֗ן וַחֲצִ֤י הַֽר־הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְעָרָ֔יו נָתַ֕תִּי לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִ֖יוְלַגָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And the land the this we took possession of at the time the that; from Aroer which [is] by [the] wadi of Arnon, and half [the] hill country of the Gilead and its cities I gave to the Reubenite[s] and to the Gadite[s].

en.L: And this land we took possession of at that time; from Aroer, which [is] by the wadi of Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead and its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
en.B: When we took possession of this land at that time, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites the stretch from Aroer beside the Arnon Valley, and half of the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
en.R: When we took over this land, I gave part of it to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. Their land started at the town of Aroer by the Arnon River and included half of the hill country of Gilead and its towns.

es.L: Y esta tierra la tomamos en posesión en aquel tiempo; desde Aroer, que [está] junto al torrente del Arnón, y la mitad de la región montañosa de Galaad y sus ciudades, [las] di a los rubenitas y a los gaditas.
es.B: Cuando en aquel tiempo tomamos posesión de esta tierra, di a los rubenitas y a los gaditas la franja que va desde Aroer, junto al valle del Arnón, y la mitad de la región montañosa de Galaad con sus poblaciones.
es.R: Cuando tomamos esta tierra, les di una parte a las tribus de Rubén y Gad. Su tierra empezaba en el pueblo de Aroer, junto al río Arnón, e incluía la mitad de la región de colinas de Galaad con sus pueblos.

fr.L: Et ce pays, nous en avons pris possession en ce temps-là ; depuis Aroër, qui [est] près du torrent de l’Arnon, et la moitié de la montagne de Galaad et ses villes, je [les] ai donnés aux Rubénites et aux Gadites.
fr.B: Lorsque nous avons pris possession de ce pays, en ce temps-là, j’ai donné aux Rubénites et aux Gadites la contrée qui part d’Aroër, au bord de la vallée de l’Arnon, et la moitié de la montagne de Galaad avec ses villes.
fr.R: Quand nous avons pris ce pays, j’en ai donné une partie aux tribus de Ruben et de Gad. Leur territoire commençait à la ville d’Aroër, près de la rivière Arnon, et comprenait la moitié des collines de Galaad avec leurs villes.

sw.L: Na nchi hii tuliimiliki wakati ule; kutoka Aroeri, ulio kando ya korongo la Arnoni, na nusu ya nchi ya milima ya Gileadi na miji yake, niliwapa Wareubeni na Wagadi.
sw.B: Tulipoimiliki nchi hii wakati ule, niliwapa Wareubeni na Wagadi eneo linaloanzia Aroeri kando ya Bonde la Arnoni, pamoja na nusu ya nchi ya milima ya Gileadi na miji yake.
sw.R: Tulipoichukua nchi hii, niliwapa makabila ya Reubeni na Gadi sehemu yake. Nchi yao ilianzia mji wa Aroeri karibu na Mto Arnoni, na ilijumuisha nusu ya nchi ya vilima ya Gileadi pamoja na miji yake.

ko.L: 그리고 그때에 우리가 이 땅을 차지했다. 아르논 골짜기 곁에 있는 아로엘에서부터 길르앗 산지 절반과 그 성읍들을 나는 르우벤 사람과 갓 사람에게 주었다.

decisions.choice: half the hill country of Gilead: the southern part, up to the Jabbok
decisions.reason: Gilead was divided. Its southern half went to Reuben and Gad (verse 16; Joshua 13:24-25), and the rest to the half-tribe of Manasseh (verse 13).

decisions.choice: I gave: Moses carries out the request of Numbers 32
decisions.reason: Reuben and Gad had asked for this land because it suited their herds, and Moses granted it on condition that their fighting men crossed the Jordan with the other tribes (Numbers 32:1-33; verses 18-20 here).

decisions.choice: When we took possession ..., I gave
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "this land" first and has two main verbs. Balanced and Readable make the first clause a time clause and set the giving of the land as the main statement.

decisions.choice: all the region of Argob ...: the start of an aside that runs through verse 14
decisions.reason: The main accent of the verse falls after "Manasseh". What follows explains the region's old name and how Jair took it, a note like those in verses 9 and 11, which ends with "to this day" in verse 14.

decisions.choice: as to all Bashan, that is called: all that part of Bashan is called
alternatives: the whole region of Argob, belonging to all Bashan
decisions.reason: The phrase "as to all Bashan" can mean that Argob belonged to Bashan or that it stands for the whole of it. "That" can point to Bashan ("all that Bashan") or begin a new clause ("it is called"). Either way the land of Argob is the land of the Rephaim.

decisions.choice: the half-tribe of Manasseh: the families of Manasseh settled east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Part of the tribe of Manasseh, the clans of Machir and Jair, took land east of the Jordan (Numbers 32:33, 39-42); the rest of the tribe settled west of it (Joshua 17:1-6).

decisions.choice: land of Rephaim: once held by the Rephaim
decisions.reason: As verse 11 says, Og was the last of the Rephaim, so his land kept their name (2:20).

decisions.choice: parenthesis opening here and closing at the end of verse 14
decisions.reason: As in verses 9 and 11, the aside is set in parentheses. It begins in this verse and ends in the next. Balanced puts "to the half-tribe of Manasseh" first, so that the aside can follow straight after the end of the main sentence.

en.R: Jair, from the tribe of Manasseh, captured the whole area of Argob, up to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He named these towns of Bashan after himself. They are still called Havvoth-jair, which means the villages of Jair.)

es.B: Jaír, descendiente de Manasés, tomó toda la región de Argob hasta la frontera de los guesuritas y los maacateos, y dio su propio nombre a esos lugares de Basán: Havot-jaír, como todavía se llaman hoy.)

fr.R: Jaïr, de la tribu de Manassé, a conquis toute la région d’Argob, jusqu’à la frontière des Gueshourites et des Maakatites. Il a donné son nom à ces villes du Bashân. On les appelle encore Havvoth-Jaïr, ce qui veut dire “les villages de Jaïr”.)

vi.L: Giai-rơ, con cháu Ma-na-se, đã lấy cả miền Ạt-gốp cho đến biên giới của người Ghê-su-rơ và người Ma-a-ca, và đã đặt tên cho chúng, [tức] Ba-san, theo tên mình: Ha-vốt Giai-rơ, cho đến ngày nay.)
vi.B: Giai-rơ, thuộc dòng dõi Ma-na-se, chiếm cả miền Ạt-gốp cho đến biên giới của người Ghê-su-rơ và người Ma-a-ca, rồi lấy tên mình đặt cho các nơi ấy ở Ba-san là Ha-vốt Giai-rơ, và cho đến ngày nay các nơi ấy vẫn mang tên đó.)
vi.R: Giai-rơ, thuộc chi tộc Ma-na-se, đã chiếm cả miền Ạt-gốp, cho đến biên giới của người Ghê-su-rơ và người Ma-a-ca. Ông lấy tên mình đặt cho các thị trấn ấy ở Ba-san. Cho đến ngày nay các thị trấn ấy vẫn được gọi là Ha-vốt Giai-rơ, nghĩa là các làng của Giai-rơ.)

decisions.choice: Jair son of Manasseh: a descendant of Manasseh
decisions.reason: "Son" here means descendant. Jair belonged to the line of Manasseh (Numbers 32:41; 1 Chronicles 2:21-22).

decisions.choice: Havvoth-jair: "the villages of Jair"
decisions.reason: The first part of the name means tent villages or settlements. The same name is given to Jair's towns in Numbers 32:41 and Judges 10:4.

decisions.choice: the Geshurites and the Maacathites: small kingdoms on the edge of Bashan
decisions.reason: Geshur and Maacah lay north and west of Bashan, toward Mount Hermon, and were not driven out (Joshua 12:5; 13:13). David later married a princess of Geshur (2 Samuel 3:3).

decisions.choice: called them, Bashan ...: named the places of Bashan; "to this day" looks back from a later time
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to the towns of the region, and "the Bashan" stands beside it to say where they were. "To this day" shows that the note speaks from a time when the name was long in use.

decisions.choice: of the line of Manasseh; these places in Bashan / these towns of Bashan; Readable "which means the villages of Jair"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "son" means descendant, and say what "them" refers to. Readable gives the meaning of the name.

decisions.choice: "Giai-rơ", "người Ghê-su-rơ", "người Ma-a-ca", "Ha-vốt Giai-rơ"
decisions.reason: The forms of Joshua 12:5, Judges 10:4 and 1 Chronicles 2:23 for the same places and people.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Ma-na-se" (L)
decisions.reason: "son of" here means a descendant of Manasseh (meaning decision), so Literal says "con cháu" rather than "con trai".

decisions.choice: Readable explains the name with "야일의 마을들이라는 뜻의"
decisions.reason: As the English Readable does and as Judges 10:4 explains the same name in Korean; no quotation marks are added, since the verse already sits inside Moses' speech.

sw.L: Na Wareubeni na Wagadi niliwapa kutoka Gileadi hadi korongo la Arnoni, katikati ya korongo na mpaka [wake], na hadi Yaboki, lile korongo, mpaka wa wana wa Amoni,
sw.B: Wareubeni na Wagadi niliwapa nchi inayoanzia Gileadi hadi Bonde la Arnoni, mpaka wake ukipita katikati ya bonde, na kuendelea hadi Mto Yaboki, mpaka wa Waamoni,
sw.R: Makabila ya Reubeni na Gadi niliwapa nchi kutoka Gileadi hadi Mto Arnoni. Katikati ya bonde la mto huo ndipo palikuwa mpaka wao wa kusini. Nchi yao ilifika hadi Mto Yaboki, uliokuwa mpaka wa Waamoni.

ko.L: 그리고 르우벤 사람과 갓 사람에게 나는 길르앗에서부터 아르논 골짜기까지, 곧 골짜기 가운데를 경계로 하여, 암몬 자손의 경계인 얍복 골짜기까지 주었다.
ko.B: 르우벤 지파와 갓 지파에게는 길르앗에서부터 아르논 골짜기까지의 땅을 주었는데, 그 골짜기의 한가운데가 경계였고, 암몬 사람들의 경계인 얍복강까지 이르렀다.
ko.R: 르우벤 지파와 갓 지파에게는 길르앗에서부터 아르논 강까지의 땅을 주었습니다. 그 강 골짜기의 한가운데가 그들의 남쪽 경계였습니다. 그들의 땅은 암몬 사람들의 경계인 얍복강까지 이르렀습니다.

vi.L: Và tôi đã ban cho người Ru-bên và người Gát từ Ga-la-át cho đến khe Ạt-nôn, giữa khe làm ranh giới, và cho đến khe Gia-bốc, ranh giới của con cháu Am-môn,
vi.B: Tôi ban cho người Ru-bên và người Gát vùng đất từ Ga-la-át đến thung lũng Ạt-nôn, lấy giữa thung lũng làm ranh giới, và cho đến sông Gia-bốc là ranh giới của người Am-môn,
vi.R: Tôi ban cho chi tộc Ru-bên và chi tộc Gát vùng đất từ Ga-la-át xuống đến sông Ạt-nôn. Giữa thung lũng sông ấy là ranh giới phía nam của họ. Đất của họ trải đến tận sông Gia-bốc, là ranh giới của người Am-môn.

decisions.choice: the middle of the wadi and border: the middle of the valley as the border
decisions.reason: "And border" says that the line ran along the middle of the Arnon valley. The same wording is used in Joshua 13:9, 16.

decisions.choice: the Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites: the upper Jabbok on the east
decisions.reason: The upper Jabbok runs north past Rabbah before turning west to the Jordan, and that stretch marked the edge of Ammon's land (Numbers 21:24; Joshua 12:2).

decisions.choice: from Gilead: from the part of Gilead given to them
decisions.reason: The land runs south from Gilead, meaning the half of Gilead in verse 12, to the Arnon.

decisions.choice: their southern border
decisions.reason: Readable adds "southern", since the Arnon was the south edge of their land (verse 12).

source.text: וְהָֽעֲרָבָ֖ה וְהַיַּרְדֵּ֣ן וּגְבֻ֑ל מִכִּנֶּ֗רֶת וְעַ֨ד יָ֤ם הָֽעֲרָבָה֙ יָ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לַח תַּ֛חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַפִּסְגָּ֖ה מִזְרָֽחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: and the Arabah and the Jordan and border, from Chinnereth and as far as [the] sea of the Arabah, [the] sea of the salt, under [the] slopes of the Pisgah eastward.

en.L: and the Arabah, with the Jordan as [its] border, from Chinnereth as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah toward the east.
en.B: and also the Arabah, with the Jordan as its border, from Chinnereth down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
en.R: Their land also included the Jordan Valley east of the river, from Lake Chinnereth, which is the Sea of Galilee, down to the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.

es.L: y el Arabá, con el Jordán como [su] límite, desde Quinéret hasta el mar del Arabá, el mar Salado, al pie de las laderas del Pisga hacia el oriente.
es.B: y también el Arabá, con el Jordán como frontera, desde Quinéret hasta el mar del Arabá, el mar Salado, al pie de las laderas del Pisga, al este.
es.R: Su tierra también incluía el valle del Jordán al este del río, desde el lago de Quinéret, que es el mar de Galilea, hasta el mar Muerto, al pie de las laderas del monte Pisga.

fr.L: et l’Araba, avec le Jourdain pour limite, depuis Kinnéreth jusqu’à la mer de l’Araba, la mer Salée, sous les pentes du Pisga vers l’orient.
fr.B: et aussi l’Araba, avec le Jourdain pour frontière, depuis Kinnéreth jusqu’à la mer de l’Araba, la mer Salée, au pied des pentes du Pisga, à l’est.
fr.R: Leur pays comprenait aussi la vallée du Jourdain, à l’est du fleuve, depuis le lac de Kinnéreth, c’est-à-dire la mer de Galilée, jusqu’à la mer Morte, au pied des pentes du mont Pisga.

sw.L: na Araba, pamoja na Yordani kuwa mpaka [wake], kutoka Kinerethi hadi bahari ya Araba, Bahari ya Chumvi, chini ya miteremko ya Pisga upande wa mashariki.
sw.B: na pia Araba, Mto Yordani ukiwa mpaka wake, kutoka Kinerethi hadi Bahari ya Araba, yaani Bahari ya Chumvi, chini ya miteremko ya Pisga upande wa mashariki.
sw.R: Nchi yao ilijumuisha pia bonde la Yordani upande wa mashariki wa mto, kutoka Ziwa Kinerethi, yaani Bahari ya Galilaya, hadi Bahari Mfu, chini ya miteremko ya Mlima Pisga.

ko.L: 또 아라바와 요단과 [그] 경계, 곧 긴네렛에서부터 아라바 바다, 곧 염해까지, 동쪽으로 비스가 산비탈 아래까지이다.
ko.B: 또 요단강을 경계로 하는 아라바도 주었는데, 그 땅은 긴네렛에서부터 동쪽 비스가 산비탈 아래 있는 아라바 바다, 곧 염해까지였다.
ko.R: 그들의 땅에는 요단강 동쪽의 요단 골짜기도 들어 있었습니다. 그 땅은 갈릴리 호수인 긴네렛에서부터 비스가 산비탈 아래에 있는 사해까지 이르렀습니다.

vi.L: và A-ra-ba, với sông Giô-đanh làm ranh giới, từ Ki-nê-rết cho đến biển A-ra-ba, tức Biển Muối, dưới các sườn núi Phích-ga về phía đông.
vi.B: và cả A-ra-ba, với sông Giô-đanh làm ranh giới, từ Ki-nê-rết xuống đến biển A-ra-ba, tức là Biển Muối, dưới chân các sườn núi Phích-ga về phía đông.
vi.R: Đất của họ cũng gồm thung lũng Giô-đanh ở phía đông sông, từ hồ Ki-nê-rết, tức là Biển Ga-li-lê, xuống đến Biển Chết, dưới chân các sườn núi Phích-ga.

decisions.choice: the Arabah with the Jordan as border: the eastern side of the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea. The part given to the eastern tribes ran along the river, which formed their western border (Joshua 13:27).

decisions.choice: Chinnereth, the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea: the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Chinnereth is the lake later called the Sea of Galilee (Numbers 34:11; Joshua 12:3). The sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, is the Dead Sea (Genesis 14:3; Joshua 3:16).

decisions.choice: the slopes of Pisgah: the hillsides above the north-east end of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Pisgah is the ridge from which Moses will look over the land (verse 27). Its slopes run down to the shore on the east side.

decisions.choice: the Jordan Valley; Lake Chinnereth, which is the Sea of Galilee; the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Readable uses the names a reader is likely to know, and says that the land lay east of the river.

decisions.choice: "Ki-nê-rết", "Biển Muối" (L, B); "hồ Ki-nê-rết, tức là Biển Ga-li-lê", "Biển Chết" (R)
decisions.reason: "Ki-nê-rết" as Joshua 13:27; "Biển Muối" translates the Hebrew name, and Readable uses the names a reader knows today, as Joshua 12:3 does.

decisions.choice: "긴네렛" for Chinnereth; "아라바 바다, 곧 염해" (Literal, Balanced) and "사해" (Readable) for the Salt Sea
decisions.reason: As the Korean Joshua names them; Readable gives the familiar modern names, adding "갈릴리 호수" as the English Readable does.

source.text: וָאֲצַ֣ו אֶתְכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֗ם נָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־הָאָ֤רֶץ הַזֹּאת֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ חֲלוּצִ֣ים תַּֽעַבְר֗וּ לִפְנֵ֛י אֲחֵיכֶ֥ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל־בְּנֵי־חָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And I commanded you at the time the that, saying, Yahweh your God has given to you the land the this to possess it; armed you will cross over before your brothers, [the] sons of Israel, all [the] sons of strength.

en.L: And I commanded you at that time, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land to take possession of it. Armed, you shall cross over before your brothers, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, all [the] sons of strength.
en.B: At that time I gave you this command: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land to possess. But every fighting man among you is to cross over armed, going ahead of your fellow Israelites.
en.R: At that time I gave an order to the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. I said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land to be your own. But all your soldiers must take their weapons and cross the river ahead of your fellow Israelites.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:les|os}} mandé en aquel tiempo, diciendo: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado esta tierra para tomar posesión de ella. Armados {{plural_you:pasarán|pasaréis}} delante de {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}}, los hijos de Israel, todos [los] hijos de valor.
es.B: En aquel tiempo {{plural_you:les|os}} di esta orden: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado esta tierra para que sea {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}. Pero todos los guerreros de entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} pasarán armados al frente de {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}} israelitas.
es.R: En ese tiempo di una orden a las tribus de Rubén, de Gad y a la media tribu de Manasés. Les dije: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado esta tierra para que sea {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}. Pero todos {{plural_you:sus soldados|vuestros soldados}} tienen que tomar las armas y cruzar el río delante de {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}} israelitas.

fr.L: Et je vous ai commandé en ce temps-là, en disant : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous a donné ce pays pour en prendre possession. Armés, vous passerez devant vos frères, les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, tous [les] fils de vaillance.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, je vous ai donné cet ordre : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous a donné ce pays pour que vous le possédiez. Mais tous les hommes de guerre parmi vous passeront en armes à la tête de vos frères israélites.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, j’ai donné un ordre aux tribus de Ruben, de Gad et à la moitié de la tribu de Manassé. Je leur ai dit : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous a donné ce pays pour qu’il soit à vous. Mais tous vos soldats doivent prendre leurs armes et traverser le fleuve devant vos frères israélites.

sw.L: Nami niliwaamuru wakati ule, nikisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu amewapa nchi hii ili kuimiliki. Mkiwa na silaha mtavuka mbele ya ndugu zenu, wana wa Israeli, ninyi nyote mlio wana wa uhodari.
sw.B: Wakati huo niliwapa agizo hili: '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu amewapa nchi hii mwimiliki. Lakini kila mwanamume wa vita miongoni mwenu atavuka akiwa na silaha, akiwatangulia ndugu zenu Waisraeli.
sw.R: Wakati huo niliyaamuru makabila ya Reubeni, Gadi na nusu ya Manase. Niliwaambia, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu amewapa nchi hii iwe yenu. Lakini askari wenu wote lazima wachukue silaha zao na kuvuka mto wakiwatangulia ndugu zenu Waisraeli.

ko.L: 그리고 그때에 나는 너희에게 명령하여 말했다. '너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅을 너희에게 주어 차지하게 하셨다. 너희 모든 용사는 무장하고 너희 형제 이스라엘 자손 앞에서 건너가라.
ko.B: 그때에 나는 너희에게 이렇게 명령했다. '너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅을 너희에게 주어 차지하게 하셨다. 그러나 너희 가운데 싸울 수 있는 남자는 모두 무장하고 너희 동족 이스라엘 백성보다 앞장서서 건너가야 한다.
ko.R: 그때에 저는 르우벤 지파와 갓 지파와 므낫세 반 지파에게 명령했습니다. '여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅을 여러분에게 주어 여러분의 것이 되게 하셨습니다. 그러나 여러분의 군인들은 모두 무기를 들고 여러분의 동족 이스라엘 사람들보다 앞서 요단강을 건너가야 합니다.

vi.L: Và vào lúc ấy tôi đã truyền cho các ngươi rằng: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi đã ban cho các ngươi xứ này để chiếm hữu nó. Hãy trang bị vũ khí và đi qua trước anh em các ngươi là con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, hết thảy những người mạnh sức.
vi.B: Lúc ấy tôi đã truyền cho anh em: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã ban cho anh em xứ này để chiếm hữu. Nhưng tất cả những người lính chiến trong anh em phải mang vũ khí đi qua sông trước những người đồng bào Y-sơ-ra-ên của mình.
vi.R: Lúc ấy tôi đã truyền lệnh cho các chi tộc Ru-bên, Gát và nửa chi tộc Ma-na-se. Tôi nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã ban cho anh em xứ này làm của riêng. Nhưng tất cả binh lính của anh em phải mang vũ khí và đi qua sông trước những người đồng bào Y-sơ-ra-ên của mình.

decisions.choice: you: the tribes east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: "You" is plural and means Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, to whom the land had just been given (verses 12-13). Moses retells the agreement of Numbers 32:20-32.

decisions.choice: armed: equipped and ready for battle
decisions.reason: The word describes men stripped for action and armed for war (Numbers 32:21, 29; Joshua 4:13).

decisions.choice: all the sons of strength: all the fighting men
decisions.reason: A "son of strength" is a capable, able-bodied man fit for war. The phrase says who must cross: not everyone, but every man able to fight.

decisions.choice: your brothers, the sons of Israel: the other tribes
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is a word for kinsmen. Here it names the rest of Israel, the tribes still to receive land west of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: every fighting man among you / all your soldiers; your fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move "all the sons of strength" to the front of the command, which shows who must go. "Your fellow Israelites" gives "your brothers, the sons of Israel" in one phrase. Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh; cross the river
decisions.reason: Readable names the people Moses addressed and says what was to be crossed.

decisions.choice: "hết thảy những người mạnh sức" (L)
decisions.reason: "sons of strength" are the fighting men (meaning decision); Literal keeps "mạnh sức" without the Hebrew "sons", which would read as real sons in Vietnamese.

decisions.choice: "용사" for "sons of strength"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom means fighting men, as the meaning decision says; "용사" is the Korean word for a valiant fighting man and keeps the sense without an unnatural genitive.

source.text: רַ֠ק נְשֵׁיכֶ֣ם וְטַפְּכֶם֮ וּמִקְנֵכֶם֒ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי־מִקְנֶ֥ה רַ֖ב לָכֶ֑ם יֵֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Only your wives and your little ones and your livestock — I know that much livestock [is] to you — will remain in your cities which I have given to you,

en.L: Only your wives and your little ones and your livestock — I know that you have much livestock — shall remain in your cities which I have given you,
en.B: Only your wives and children and your livestock — and I know how much livestock you have — are to stay behind in the towns I have given you,
en.R: Only your wives, your children and your animals may stay in the towns I have given you. I know you have a lot of animals.

es.L: Solo {{plural_you:sus mujeres|vuestras mujeres}} y {{plural_you:sus pequeños|vuestros pequeños}} y {{plural_you:su ganado|vuestro ganado}} —yo sé que {{plural_you:ustedes tienen|tenéis}} mucho ganado— se quedarán en {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado,
es.B: Solo {{plural_you:sus mujeres|vuestras mujeres}}, {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} y {{plural_you:su ganado|vuestro ganado}} —y sé cuánto ganado {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}— se quedarán en las poblaciones que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado,
es.R: Solo {{plural_you:sus esposas|vuestras esposas}}, {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} y {{plural_you:sus animales|vuestros animales}} pueden quedarse en los pueblos que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado. Sé que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} muchos animales.

fr.L: Seulement vos femmes, vos petits enfants et votre bétail — je sais que vous avez beaucoup de bétail — resteront dans vos villes que je vous ai données,
fr.B: Seuls vos femmes et vos enfants, ainsi que votre bétail — et je sais combien vous avez de bétail —, resteront dans les villes que je vous ai données,
fr.R: Seuls vos femmes, vos enfants et vos animaux peuvent rester dans les villes que je vous ai données. Je sais que vous avez beaucoup d’animaux.

sw.L: Ila wake zenu, na watoto wenu wadogo, na mifugo yenu — najua kwamba mna mifugo mingi — watabaki katika miji yenu niliyowapa,
sw.B: Ni wake zenu na watoto wenu tu, pamoja na mifugo yenu — nami najua mna mifugo mingi kiasi gani — watakaobaki katika miji niliyowapa,
sw.R: Wake zenu, watoto wenu na wanyama wenu tu ndio wanaoweza kubaki katika miji niliyowapa. Najua mna wanyama wengi.

ko.L: 다만 너희 아내들과 너희 어린것들과 너희 가축은 — 너희에게 가축이 많은 줄을 내가 안다 — 내가 너희에게 준 너희 성읍들에 머물 것이다.
ko.B: 다만 너희 아내와 아이들과 가축은 — 너희에게 가축이 많다는 것을 나도 안다 — 내가 너희에게 준 성읍들에 남아 있어도 된다.
ko.R: 다만 여러분의 아내와 아이들과 가축은 제가 여러분에게 준 성읍들에 남아 있어도 됩니다. 여러분에게 가축이 많다는 것을 저도 압니다.

vi.L: Chỉ vợ các ngươi, con nhỏ các ngươi và súc vật các ngươi, (tôi biết các ngươi có nhiều súc vật,) sẽ ở lại trong các thành của các ngươi mà tôi đã ban cho các ngươi,

decisions.choice: gives rest: gives a settled, secure life in the land, free from enemies
decisions.reason: Rest is God's promised gift once the land is won (12:9-10; 25:19). Joshua 22:4 tells how the eastern tribes were sent home when it came.

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: here the land west of the river
decisions.reason: Moses speaks on the east side, so "beyond the Jordan" here means the land of Canaan that the other tribes are still to enter, unlike verse 8.

decisions.choice: his possession: the land each one holds as his own
decisions.reason: The word means what is taken and held as one's property, the family's share of land.

decisions.choice: as he has granted it to you / as he has given you rest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "as to you" means: the eastern tribes had already been given rest.

decisions.choice: Stay with them ... Wait until ...; west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence and supplies the verbs that link it to verse 18. It also says on which side of the river the land lies.

decisions.choice: "ban sự yên nghỉ" (L, B); "cho được yên ổn" (R)
decisions.reason: Rest here is a settled, secure life in the land, free from enemies (meaning decision), not a pause from work; Readable says "yên ổn" to make that plain.

decisions.choice: "안식을 주다" for "give rest"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes a settled, secure life in the land; "안식" carries that weight and links with the rest promised in the land elsewhere in Deuteronomy and in Hebrews 4 in Korean.

records.literal_gloss: And Joshua I commanded at the time the that, saying, your eyes [are] the [ones] seeing all that did Yahweh your God to [the] two the kings the these; so will do Yahweh to all the kingdoms which you [are] crossing there.

en.L: And Joshua I commanded at that time, saying, 'Your eyes [are] the ones that have seen all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has done to these two kings; so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.
en.B: At that time I commanded Joshua: 'Your own eyes have seen everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to these two kings. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will deal in the same way with every kingdom you are crossing over to.
en.R: At that time I gave Joshua orders. I told him, 'You saw for yourself what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to these two kings. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will do that to every kingdom on the other side of the river, where you are going.

es.L: Y a Josué mandé en aquel tiempo, diciendo: “Tus ojos [son] los que han visto todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:el Dios de ustedes|vuestro Dios}} ha hecho a estos dos reyes; así hará {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a todos los reinos a los que tú vas a pasar.
es.B: En aquel tiempo di esta orden a Josué: “Tus propios ojos han visto todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:el Dios de ustedes|vuestro Dios}} hizo a estos dos reyes. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará lo mismo con todos los reinos a los que vas a pasar.
es.R: En ese tiempo le di órdenes a Josué. Le dije: “Tú mismo viste lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:el Dios de ustedes|vuestro Dios}} les hizo a estos dos reyes. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará lo mismo con todos los reinos al otro lado del río, adonde vas.

fr.L: Et à Josué j’ai commandé en ce temps-là, en disant : “Tes yeux [sont] ceux qui ont vu tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu a fait à ces deux rois ; ainsi fera {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à tous les royaumes où tu vas passer.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, j’ai donné cet ordre à Josué : “Tes propres yeux ont vu tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu a fait à ces deux rois. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} traitera de même tous les royaumes vers lesquels tu vas passer.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, j’ai donné des ordres à Josué. Je lui ai dit : “Tu as vu toi-même ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu a fait à ces deux rois. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera la même chose à tous les royaumes de l’autre côté du fleuve, là où tu vas.
